cards.title: A CV can now be read in three independent ways
cards.claim: Post-merge, can read CV ⇒ owner OR public-token OR same organization_id. Any one branch in canViewCV returning true grants access.
cards.whyItMatters: Every reader of cvs must route through canViewCV, or it silently skips the new branch. The blast radius is every place that pulls a CV from the DB.

items.desc: reads cv via raw findUnique — does not call canViewCV

sections.label: Check
sections.text: Do all read paths route through canViewCV? export.ts is in the blast radius but does a raw findUnique.

cards.title: Org sharing modeled as a column on cvs, not a join table
cards.claim: organization_id lives directly on cvs. There is no cv_org_shares join table, no per-recipient ACL, no support for multiple orgs.
cards.whyItMatters: Caps the model at one organization per CV. A second org or per-member permissions later would need a migration off the column model.

items.desc: would allow per-user grants within an org

sections.label: Check
sections.text: Is single-org-per-CV the long-term model? Multi-org or per-recipient ACL needed later?

cards.title: Read-permission rule centralized in canViewCV
cards.claim: Rather than scattering checks at each reader, the PR adds the new branch in one place. Every reader is expected to call canViewCV.
cards.whyItMatters: Centralization is correct — but only if every reader actually goes through it. One bypass and the rule is fiction.

items.desc: is a reader, doesn't call canViewCV

sections.label: Check
sections.text: Is the export.ts bypass intentional or missed?

cards.title: Service writers do not enforce ownership
cards.claim: shareCVWithOrg accepts any actor and writes organization_id to any CV. The API route runs requireAuth — authentication, not ownership.
cards.whyItMatters: The gate location is unclear. UI hides the share action for non-owners; server only verifies auth. A direct curl from any logged-in user can share a colleague's CV with the colleague's org.

sections.label: Check
sections.text: Should ownership live in the service or the API route? The PR is internally inconsistent — revoke checks, share doesn't.

cards.title: Existing CVs enter the new world with organization_id = NULL
cards.claim: The migration adds a nullable column. No backfill statement. ~12,418 pre-existing rows land in the new permission code path with organization_id = NULL.
cards.whyItMatters: canViewCV compares cv.organization_id === user.organizationId. For users whose own organizationId is NULL (system actors, cron jobs, seed admins), NULL === NULL is true — granting access to every legacy CV.

items.desc: ADD COLUMN ... NULL — no DEFAULT, no backfill

sections.label: Check
sections.text: Acceptable for legacy CVs to enter the new code path as NULL? Acceptable for NULL-org actors to satisfy the new branch?

cards.title: Duplicate inherits the source's organization, not the actor's
cards.claim: duplicateCV copies organization_id from the source CV. The actor's own organizationId is ignored.
cards.whyItMatters: Now that non-owners can interact with org-shared CVs (via ShareMenu), a duplicator who is a member but not owner creates a copy that lives in the source's org — under the duplicator's userId. Ownership and org membership for the new CV may disagree with the duplicator's intent.

items.desc: duplicate now reachable from org-shared context

sections.label: Check
sections.text: Should duplicate inherit source.organization_id or actor.organizationId? Are cross-user duplicates expected?

cards.title: revokeOrgSharing clears organization_id but leaves publicTokenId untouched
cards.claim: Revoke only writes organization_id = NULL. cv.publicTokenId is a separate field set by the existing share-link flow and is not modified.
cards.whyItMatters: The word "revoke" in the UI may imply a stronger guarantee than the implementation provides. A CV that was once public-shared still loads via /share/<token> after org revoke.

sections.label: Check
sections.text: Should revoke also invalidate / rotate the public token? Or are these orthogonal sharing channels by design?

cards.title: Tests prove the happy path; the contradicted assumptions are untested
cards.claim: Two specs: admin shares with own org; member reads after share. No specs for the behaviours the PR potentially breaks.
cards.whyItMatters: Whatever the PR adds is covered. Whatever the PR risks is not. A regression in an unchanged sibling path won't fail CI.

oneLiner: Recruiting agencies can now share candidate CVs with their organization. A new nullable column on cvs gates this, and the existing read-permission check learns a third branch.

modelDeltas.title: Organization-scoped access
modelDeltas.before: A CV is readable by owner checks or public token checks.
modelDeltas.after: A CV can also be readable through organization membership when organization_id is set.

modelDeltas.title: Sharing writer
modelDeltas.before: No service-level writer assigns a CV to an organization.
modelDeltas.after: shareCVWithOrg and revokeOrgSharing become the write path for organization sharing state.

or intentionally has a stronger gate.

assumptions.text: Service writers are only reachable from API routes that already proved ownership or admin authority.
Duplicating a CV should not accidentally copy organization sharing unless that is intended product behavior.
